recommendation_issues.problem: Two server-side counters per key, strict per-device ordering and cascading 'tekrar dene' add state and a head-of-line stall: one record stuck on 'tekrar dene' holds back every later record of that phone, against the 95%-in-24h target. Smaller fix: do not sign online requests (downloads, time-certificate refresh) with the App Attest key; authenticate them with a device token issued at registration, so only records consume the counter. For records, require the counter to be unused for that key (unique (device, counter) on the record row) instead of greater than the last; replay is already blocked by the unique record id, the unique (device, sequence) and the signature over the exact bytes, and node-app-attest accepts the reference signCount as an input. The reason for departing from Apple's step 5 is written into the plan. The open question's Secure Enclave key, bound once with App Attest, removes the counter entirely and is the cleaner long-term option.

The trade-off omits two costs of the Play Integrity-only pick. Standard-request tokens can only be decrypted on Google's servers (local decryption needs the app on Google Play), so every Android registration makes a server-to-Google call with a service-account token and spends one of 10,000 daily decryptions. The server also loses its only direct proof that the Android key is hardware-backed, so the 'anahtar turu' field at line 786 becomes app-reported. The default should follow line 857: Play track adopted, Play Integrity only; GitHub only, key attestation only (checked on the server without Google calls or quota), accepting the custom verifier and root upkeep.

Removing the software key leaves no signing key for an iPhone whose App Attest attestation fails with a non-retryable error (Apple: discard the key and create a new one), and the reactive 'add a software key when seen' would bring back @noble/curves and the r||s branch. Smaller fallback with no new package: the own native module creates a Secure Enclave P-256 key with CryptoKit (iOS 13+), signs records in DER, and the device carries the 'Cihaz dogrulanmadi' label; the server already verifies DER. Optionally the Android Keystore key is generated in the same own module that signs, rather than relying on the key parameters of an alpha package.

The per-device 'ortam' column is redundant: node-app-attest refuses development-environment keys unless allowDevelopmentEnvironment is set and returns the environment, so one production server setting covers it. The receipt only feeds Apple's fraud metric, which the same research advises against adding, so storing it is optional. The counter columns depend on the S08-04 choice: with the uniqueness rule the counter sits on the record row, not the device row.

'Dogrulama sonraki acilista kendiliginden yeniden denenir' spends a token preparation on every app open while the day's quota is exhausted, eating into the next day as well. Cap it at one retry per device per day with exponential backoff, which Google's error page advises.

misses.finding: The verification list names server tools for key attestation and App Attest but nothing for Play Integrity, which line 78 relies on. @expo/app-integrity uses standard requests, whose tokens can only be decrypted on Google's servers: the server needs a service account in the Cloud project, an OAuth access token with the playintegrity scope and a decodeIntegrityToken call per registration, each counted against the 10,000/day decryption limit. Local decryption is offered only to apps on Google Play. If the Cloud project sits under an organization created on or after 3 May 2024, the baseline policy blocks creating service-account keys, the simple way for a self-hosted server to authenticate.

misses.recommendation_tr: İmza doğrulama satırına Play Integrity'nin sunucu adımı eklenir. Telefonun gönderdiği jeton sunucuda Google'ın decodeIntegrityToken ucuna gönderilip çözülür; standart istek jetonu yalnız Google'ın sunucusunda çözülebiliyor. Bunun için Google bulut projesinde bir hizmet hesabı açılır, anahtarı sunucuda gizli ayar olarak durur ve loglara yazılmaz; erişim jetonu Google'ın bakımındaki google-auth-library ile alınır, istek düz fetch ile atılır. Her çözme günlük 10.000 sınırına sayılır. Google'a ulaşılamazsa kayıt durmaz: telefon 'Cihaz doğrulanmadı' etiketiyle bağlanır, doğrulama ertesi gün yeniden denenir. Bulut projesi bir kuruluşa bağlı olmadan, kişisel hesapta açılır; 3 Mayıs 2024'ten sonra kurulan kuruluşlarda hizmet hesabı anahtarı üretimi varsayılan olarak kapalıdır. Android'de yalnız anahtar kanıtı seçilirse bu adım ve hizmet hesabı hiç gerekmez.

misses.finding: On iPhone the signing goes through @expo/app-integrity's generateAssertionAsync(keyId, challenge), which takes a string and signs over SHA256 of its UTF-8 bytes, not over arbitrary bytes. If the record is binary and passed as base64, the server must hash the base64 text exactly as sent; hashing the decoded bytes makes every iPhone record fail verification and end as 'ret'.

evidence.quote: let data = Data(challenge.utf8)
let clientDataHash = Data(SHA256.hash(data: data))
generateAssertionAsync(keyId, challenge)

misses.recommendation_tr: Kayıt bir kez tek bir metne çevrilir (ör. kayıt baytlarının base64 hali) ve telefonda, kuyrukta ve sunucuda hep bu metin olduğu gibi saklanır. iPhone onayı bu metnin UTF-8 baytları üzerinden alınır, Android imzası da aynı baytlara atılır. Sunucu metni yeniden üretmez, gelen metni özetleyip doğrular. Bunu iPhone ve Android için birer uçtan uca davranış senaryosu korur.

verdict_reason: All 10 findings re-checked against primary sources (Play Integrity verdicts/setup pages updated 2026-10-01, improvements and error pages 2026-02-26, key attestation page 2026-07-09 and the live root JSON, Apple DeviceCheck docs plus WWDC21 and WWDC26 transcripts, Expo SDK 57 docs and package source, npm registry, RFC 7518): 10 confirmed, 0 corrected, 0 refuted, 0 unverifiable. Of 12 checked_ok items, the versioned and dated ones were spot-checked; 1 is overstated (Android 7 hardware attestation, low impact). Five recommendation issues, none high: the S08-04 two-counter plus cascade-retry fix is heavier than a uniqueness rule with token-authenticated online requests; S08-03's Play Integrity-only default misses the Google-side decryption dependency and the loss of hardware-key proof; S08-10 lacks an iPhone fallback key; S08-05 adds a redundant environment column; S08-02 needs a retry cap. Two low-severity misses: the Play Integrity server decode step is absent from line 589, and the iOS module signs a UTF-8 string, not raw bytes. S08-04 is arguably high given the zero-loss target, but it is confirmed. No high-severity item is unverified and no high-severity miss remains, so the slice passes.
